siteMatches.evidenceText: 4 You’re here Building the table Work through the core explanation before applying it. 05 Building the table core concept List each distinct value in the first column and count how often it occurred to get the frequency . The frequencies must add to the number of results. Relative frequency is each frequency divided by the total. Because every result is counted in exactly one row, these must sum to 1, which is the quickest check on the whole table. Cumulative frequency is the running total: each entry is the previous cumulative value plus the current frequency. The final entry equals the total number of results. findings.detail: The site has 103 Year 11 lessons in eight folders. Coverage of the 2024 points is broad (see summary), but 13 lessons are retired by inline notices yet still live, several more teach Year 12, Extension 1 or Mathematics Standard content without a notice, and the module metadata is stale. This matches the earlier audit wording that Year 11 Advanced is "not yet a reliable implementation of the 2024 syllabus" for site structure, though the newer recall-format lessons map closely to single dotpoints.

Folders do not match the seven 2024 focus areas: algebraic-techniques-and-inequalities is a content group of Working with functions, and the probability-and-data folder mixes Year 11 lessons with retired Year 12 and Standard lessons.

Every lesson carries an old module number (m1 to m6) and site outcome codes (MAV-11-xx), not NESA codes. Probability L01 to L10 carry maths-adv-y12-m5 ids; four of them have Year 12 Module 5 titles. Many files carry a lesson id whose number differs from the file name (for example working-with-functions/lesson06 is m1-l07).
Direct and inverse variation lessons teach only n = 1; the syllabus model is y = kx^n and y = k/x^n.

Missing: sqrt(x^2) = |x| by substitution; sec, cosec and cot at 0 and 90 degrees by limiting triangles; sec = r/x, cosec = r/y, cot = x/y on a circle of radius r; the gradient function of a^x is k a^x; enlargement by replacing both x and y by x/k and y/k; the algebraic proof that P(A|B) = P(A) implies P(B|A) = P(B).
Site uses y = mx + b (syllabus y = mx + c) and csc (syllabus cosec).

limitations: No site file was changed. Page text was inspected; live interactive behaviour was not tested.
A covered action can still contain a wording or worked-solution error; this crosswalk does not replace a lesson mathematics review. Only the first-strand worked examples were recalculated.
Coverage judgements were made from section text and targeted searches, not a full line-by-line read of all 103 lessons.
